# An exact joint clipping polynomial for a triangular middle fiber

This note keeps the three clipping constraints on one actual triangle.
It provides an exact one-variable area formula, not a universal upper
bound on that formula. In particular no conjectural optimization over
triangles or sources is used as a theorem.

## 1. Ordinary geometric data

Let K be a nondegenerate triangle inside an outer triangle Delta.
Let lambda_1,lambda_2,lambda_3 be the barycentric coordinates of
Delta, with each min_K lambda_i=0. Their sum is one. Fix y in int K
and write u_i=lambda_i(y)>0. Suppose each of the caps

    C_i=K intersect {lambda_i>=u_i}

captures exactly one vertex of K strictly and has neither of the
other two vertices on its cutting line. Suppose these captured
vertices are distinct, and label them P_i accordingly.

The incidence assumption is explicit. It follows, for example,
from the separately proved sharp triangle-incidence lemma when
the three cap fractions are at most128/279, but that result need
not be invoked in order to use the present formula.

Define

    S_(ij)=lambda_i(P_j), R=S^(-1),
    a_i=(R u)_i,
    q_i=|C_i|/|K|,
    p_i=|C_j intersect C_l|/|K|, {i,j,l}={1,2,3},
    alpha_i=2u_i/S_(ii),
    beta_i=2-2a_i/R_(ii).

The matrix S is invertible, nonnegative and column-stochastic;
the a_i are the positive K-barycentric coordinates of y.

For 0<=rho<=2 let

    E_rho={xi in R^3: xi>=0, sum_i xi_i=rho,
                         S xi<=2u coordinatewise}.

Area in its affine plane is normalized so that the full simplex
{xi>=0,sum xi=rho} has area rho^2 |K|. Equivalently, map the
plane by the affine vertex map to the corresponding scaled copy
of K, and use the inherited constant area Jacobian.

## 2. The exact formula

**Theorem.** All alpha_i and beta_i lie strictly between zero
and two. Every R_(ii) is positive. For 0<=rho<=2,

    |E_rho|/|K|=rho^2
       -4 sum_i q_i [(rho-alpha_i)_+/(2-alpha_i)]^2
       +4 sum_i p_i [(rho-beta_i)_+/(2-beta_i)]^2.       (1)

Here x_+=max(x,0). The area normalization in (1) is the one just
defined; the assertion is independent of the Euclidean choice
of coordinates on the affine plane.

*Proof.* The strict one-vertex condition gives

    0<u_i<S_(ii),
    u_i>S_(ij) for j!=i.

Thus 0<alpha_i<2. In the full rho-simplex, the removed i-th
cap is S_i.xi>2u_i. Dividing xi by rho shows that, for rho<=2,
it remains a corner triangle at P_i whenever nonempty. It first
appears at rho=alpha_i. Its two edge lengths are affine multiples
of rho-alpha_i. Hence its area is a fixed positive constant times
(rho-alpha_i)_+^2. At rho=2 its area is 4q_i|K|, which proves
the negative term in (1).

Consider the intersection of the removed j-th and l-th caps.
For rho sufficiently close to two it is a triangle of positive
area: its tip is the intersection of the two cutting lines in
the interior of the rho-simplex, and its base lies on the edge
joining P_j and P_l. Neither of the other edges can supply a
positive-length boundary piece, because the j-th corner cap
does not reach the edge opposite P_j, and the l-th corner cap
does not reach the edge opposite P_l. The two remaining cutting
lines and that one original edge therefore bound the entire
intersection.

As rho decreases, each cap divided by rho shrinks monotonically
inside the corresponding original cap, because u_j,u_l>0.
The pair intersection remains a triangle until it vanishes when
the two edge-intersection points meet. It vanishes at a unique
scale beta_i in (0,2): it is positive at rho=2, while below
max(alpha_j,alpha_l)>0 at least one constituent cap is empty.

To identify this scale exactly, the common tip has

    S xi=2u+(rho-2)e_i,
    xi=2a+(rho-2)R e_i.

Its coordinate perpendicular to the base edge is
xi_i=2a_i+(rho-2)R_(ii). This is positive near rho=2 and
zero at the unique vanishing scale. Consequently R_(ii)>0
and beta_i=2-2a_i/R_(ii). In particular 0<beta_i<2.

The base edge and the two cut directions have fixed directions
as rho changes. The two edge-intersection points and the tip
depend affinely on rho and coincide when rho=beta_i. Their
triangle is therefore a translated homothetic copy with linear
scale rho-beta_i. At rho=2 its area is 4p_i|K|. This proves
the positive term in (1), including its zero part below beta_i.

Finally the triple intersection of the removed caps is empty
for rho<2: all three strict inequalities would give
sum_i(S xi)_i>2 sum_i u_i=2, whereas that sum is rho. At
rho=2 the closed triple intersection is a single point and has
zero area. Ordinary inclusion-exclusion for these three actual
sets proves (1). All cutting lines have zero area, so choosing
closed rather than open caps changes none of these identities.
QED.

## 3. Application to actual true-facet erosion

Let the continuous normals be the canonical v_1=(1,0),
v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1), and put T={v_i.x<=1}. Let K be any
triangle, t_i=h_K(-v_i), tau=sum_i t_i, and use its actual
aligned outer coordinates lambda_i=(v_i.x+t_i)/tau.

Let A,B be convex bodies satisfying B contained in T and
(A+B)/2 contained in K. Suppose each A cut
v_i.x=2v_i.y-1 is proper. The exact true-facet enclosure gives

    A contained in p+(2-rho)K,
    B contained in -p+rho K, 0<rho<2.

Put c_i=[v_i.p+(rho-1)t_i]/tau and d_i=(1+t_i)/tau. The
proper cuts and the original B support restrictions give

    c_i+d_i<2u_i,
    sum_i(c_i+d_i)=rho+3/tau.

After pulling B back into the rho-simplex in K-barycentric
coordinates, its exact three restrictions are

    xi>=0, sum xi=rho, S xi<=c+d.

Thus it is contained in E_rho, and (1) yields the rigorous bound

    |B|/|K|<=|E_rho|/|K|.                         (2)

The strict individual upper bounds and their fixed sum can be
retained for a stronger calculation; replacing them by 2u is
only a relaxation in the direction of an upper bound.

For any fixed actual K,y satisfying the incidence hypotheses,
the right side of (1) is an explicit piecewise quadratic in
rho on [0,2]. Its maximum is found by checking its breakpoints,
the two endpoints, and any stationary point of each quadratic
piece. This is an exact finite calculation for those data.
It does not establish a uniform bound over all K,y, nor does it
assert that every body in the relaxed enclosure can be completed
to the original A,B configuration or to a critical cap family.
